# STEP 1 — Complete Product Foundation, Public Website and Design System

You are building a production-minded AI Ads Manager SaaS application for ecommerce brands.

The product allows an ecommerce marketer to enter their store URL, research their brand and products, generate AI advertising creatives, iterate on them and approve final advertisements.

This is a real product build, not a static prototype.


Create a Frontend Folder & Build Everything in that Landing -> Login Signup -> Dashboard 


## A. Technology stack

Use the following fixed stack:

- Next.js App Router
- React
- TypeScript
- Tailwind CSS
- Vercel AI SDK and AI Elements
- Supabase (Postgres, Auth, Storage)
- Firecrawl
- LLM through Vercel AI Gateway
- fal.ai for image generation
- Sharp for image composition
- Vercel hosting

Use compatible current stable dependencies.

Do not introduce another frontend framework, backend framework or database.

## B. Product structure

Create two separate application areas.

### Public website

- Landing page
- Product/features page
- How it works
- Pricing placeholder or plans section only if useful
- Login
- Signup
- Forgot password
- Password reset
- Privacy and terms placeholders

### Authenticated application

- First-time onboarding
- Dashboard
- Brands
- Brand details
- Product catalog
- Campaigns
- Campaign details
- Creative library
- Creative details
- Account settings

The authenticated application will be implemented progressively in later steps, but establish its route structure and shared design system now.

## C. Landing page design

Build a complete, polished SaaS landing page.

The visual quality should resemble a serious modern B2B SaaS product, not a generic AI template.

### Navigation

Include:
- Product logo and name.
- Product.
- How it works.
- Features.
- Login.
- Get started CTA.

Use a proper responsive mobile navigation.

### Hero section

Create a compelling hero explaining the product.

Suggested headline:

"From your storefront to ads that are ready to run."

Supporting message:

"Turn your ecommerce products into on-brand advertising creatives. Research your brand, generate ads and refine every creative in one intelligent workspace."

Include:
- Store URL input.
- Generate ads CTA.
- Product dashboard preview.
- A visually compelling example of the creative workflow.

The URL input should validate basic URL format. Preserve the submitted URL for onboarding after signup when possible.

Do not pretend that a submitted URL has been researched before the backend research feature exists.

### Product demonstration

Show the product's actual intended workflow:

1. Enter your store URL.
2. Discover your products and brand identity.
3. Create advertising concepts.
4. Generate portrait creatives.
5. Review, iterate and approve.

Use carefully designed UI previews. Clearly treat example content as illustrative rather than real customer results.

### Feature sections

Create polished sections for:

- Brand intelligence.
- Product discovery.
- AI advertising strategy.
- Reference-image-based creative generation.
- Creative iteration and version history.
- Review and approval workflow.

### Creative showcase

Display an editorial-style gallery of example portrait advertising creatives.

Use original or properly licensed illustrative imagery. Do not imply these are actual generated results from the application.

### Final sections

- How it works.
- Product benefits.
- FAQ.
- Final signup CTA.
- Footer with navigation and legal links.

## D. Design system

Establish reusable design tokens for:

- Typography.
- Colors.
- Backgrounds.
- Borders.
- Radius.
- Shadows.
- Spacing.
- Buttons.
- Inputs.
- Cards.
- Dialogs.
- Toasts.
- Loading states.

Create reusable components rather than duplicating styles.

Design characteristics:

- Premium B2B SaaS.
- Clean and spacious.
- Excellent typographic hierarchy.
- Strong visual product demonstrations.
- Restrained color palette.
- Consistent interaction states.
- Responsive across desktop, tablet and mobile.

Avoid:
- Excessive gradients.
- Generic AI illustrations.
- Unnecessary glassmorphism.
- Oversized empty hero sections.
- Decorative elements that reduce usability.

## E. Route structure

Establish these routes:

Public:
- /
- /product
- /how-it-works
- /login
- /signup
- /forgot-password
- /reset-password

Authenticated:
- /onboarding
- /dashboard
- /brands
- /brands/[brandId]
- /campaigns
- /campaigns/[campaignId]
- /creatives
- /creatives/[creativeId]
- /settings

Create appropriate route groups and shared layouts.

Do not implement fake authentication. Authentication will be integrated in Step 2.

Authenticated routes can have temporary development placeholders, but must not be presented as functioning features.

## F. Code quality

- Use strict TypeScript.
- Organize components by responsibility.
- Keep business logic outside presentation components.
- Create reusable form components.
- Validate inputs.
- Avoid unnecessary dependencies.
- Avoid giant page components.
- Use accessible HTML semantics.
- Ensure responsive behavior.
- Keep the project easy to extend.

## G. Documentation requirement

Create:

docs/architecture.mmd
docs/decisions.md
docs/implementation-log.md

The architecture diagram must show the complete intended product, including authentication, frontend, agent orchestration, Firecrawl, LLM Gateway, fal.ai, Supabase database and Storage, feedback and approval.

Clearly distinguish planned components from implemented components.

Update the COMPLETE Mermaid architecture after this step and every subsequent step.

## H. Acceptance criteria

Before completing this step:

1. Run the application.
2. Verify every public navigation link.
3. Verify the landing page on desktop and mobile.
4. Verify login/signup pages have proper visual foundations, even though authentication is implemented in Step 2.
5. Verify the application route structure.
6. Run TypeScript checks.
7. Run a production build.
8. Fix all errors.

The styling issue was caused by Tailwind CSS v4 running in Next.js without the PostCSS transformation pipeline configured.

### Root Cause
1. In Tailwind v4, `@import "tailwindcss";` inside `globals.css` requires `@tailwindcss/postcss` and a `postcss.config.mjs` to be compiled into actual CSS utility classes.
2. Without `@tailwindcss/postcss`, Next.js passed `@import "tailwindcss";` through raw, causing the browser to ignore the directive and render an unstyled page (only ~2 KB of font declarations were being output).

---

### What Was Fixed
1. **Installed `@tailwindcss/postcss`**:
   Installed the official `@tailwindcss/postcss` plugin in `frontend/`.

2. **Added [postcss.config.mjs](file:///home/ankitmishralive/Desktop/Ankit%20Mishra/startup's/experiment's/cadra-ads/frontend/postcss.config.mjs)**:
   ```javascript
   const config = {
     plugins: {
       "@tailwindcss/postcss": {},
     },
   };

   export default config;
   ```

3. **Restored Custom Tokens & Utility Classes** in [globals.css](file:///home/ankitmishralive/Desktop/Ankit%20Mishra/startup's/experiment's/cadra-ads/frontend/src/app/globals.css):
   - Background grid pattern: `.bg-grid-subtle`
   - Hero glow effect: `.bg-radial-glow`
   - CTA glow effect: `.bg-radial-bottom`
   - Custom dark scrollbars and palette variables

4. **Restarted Dev Server**:
   Killed the stale dev server process that had cached the unstyled CSS and started a fresh instance on **`http://localhost:3000`**.

---

- Verified that all utility classes (`.bg-slate-950`, `.flex`, `.grid`, `.max-w-7xl`, `.border-slate-800`, etc.) and background gradients are rendered.

# Architectural Transformation: Leonardo da Vinci White Theme

The design system and layout have been completely redesigned according to the **Leonardo da Vinci Codex** aesthetic—eschewing generic AI templates, purple glows, and icon clutter in favor of timeless Renaissance drafting principles: Vitruvian proportions, delicate hairline rules, pure editorial typography, and the provided background and video media.

---

### Key Architectural Changes Implemented

1. **Entirely White & Alabaster Palette**
   - Pure white background (`#ffffff`), delicate drafting paper gridlines (`.bg-draft-grid`), and crisp charcoal/black typography.
   - Replaced all neon glows, purple pill badges, and dark card fills with fine hairline borders (`border-neutral-200` / `border-neutral-300`).
   - Clean classical serif titles (`font-serif-title`) paired with technical, monospaced drafting annotations.

2. **Complete Removal of Icons & Logos**
   - **No icons or logos**: All Lucide icons, icon badges, and graphical logo marks were eliminated across navigation, buttons, cards, forms, headers, and footers.
   - Typographic wordmark: **CADRA** in classical, architectural serif.
   - Text-first, structural navigation: `[ RETURN TO TREATISE ]`, `[ PLATE 01 ]`, `[ 01. WORKSPACE ]`, `[ CLOSE ]`.

3. **Hero Section with `hero.png` as Background**
   - [HeroSection.tsx](file:///home/ankitmishralive/Desktop/Ankit%20Mishra/startup's/experiment's/cadra-ads/frontend/src/components/public/HeroSection.tsx) now seamlessly integrates `hero.png` as the hero background with an architectural parchment overlay and subtle draft grid.
   - Minimalist, high-contrast store URL input with a solid black button: `GENERATE ADS`.
   - Technical Da Vinci study plate below demonstrating the Vitruvian proportional analysis of direct-response creatives ($1:1.618$ golden section).

4. **Login & Signup Split Layout with `video.mp4`**
